## Proposals
# Proposals — 2026-07-13

## P-2026-07-13-001: self_improvement

**Problem:** Night Shift cannot distinguish infrastructure failure from agent regression, and its eval-output parser is brittle. Tonight: 3 parse failures (DYN-20260713-2, B3 skill-gap output, reviewer TC1 — raws saved but unscored), and developer TC6 scored 0 (delta -3.60, flagged DEGRADED) while a same-night rerun scored 4.6 — the 0 was the API credit exhaustion documented in the B3 'autonomous-run-infrastructure-health' gap, not agent quality. Result: 7 consecutive RED runs (2026-06-21 through 2026-07-13) where RED is partly self-inflicted noise, eroding the signal Hero relies on.

**Solution:** Modify the Night Shift pipeline (~/.claude/agents/night-shift.md plus the B1/B2/B3 scoring scripts under ~/.claude/night-shift/): (1) add an A0 preflight that verifies API reachability/credit before any scoring phase and aborts to a distinct INFRA status if it fails; (2) classify empty or credit-error raws as INFRA_FAIL, excluded from baseline/delta math and status-color computation, listed in a separate 'infrastructure' briefing section; (3) wrap eval output in a strict JSON contract (retry once with a 'respond only with JSON' repair prompt before saving raw and marking INFRA_FAIL); (4) when duplicate runs of the same prompt_id exist in one night, use max score and flag variance instead of reporting both.

**Impact:** RED becomes reserved for genuine agent regression; false DEGRADED findings like tonight's TC6 disappear; the 3-per-night parse-failure class is either auto-repaired or cleanly quarantined; the 7-night RED streak resolves into an honest status signal Hero can act on.

**Risk:** Overly broad INFRA_FAIL classification could mask a real regression that happens to produce malformed output (an agent emitting garbage IS a failure); mitigate by requiring the raw to match known error signatures (credit/rate-limit/HTTP 5xx) before excluding it from degradation math, and always surfacing INFRA_FAIL counts in the briefing.

## P-2026-07-13-002: eval_evolution

**Problem:** Eval saturation: consecutive_all_pass=21 and all_pass_streak_days=77 (B0 metrics), with the PIVOT finding 'All canaries passing for 77 days — evals too easy.' Multiple static canaries sit at ceiling (night-shift TC1: 5.0 twice tonight, reviewer TC7: 5.0 twice tonight). Meanwhile B2 dynamic evals produced only 2 attempts tonight (one unparseable), so the eval suite is measuring memorized floor behavior, not current failure modes like the 4 capability_gaps_7d.

**Solution:** In the eval definitions under ~/.claude/night-shift/ (B1 static suite + B2 dynamic generator): retire or graduate canaries that have scored ≥4.8 for 21+ consecutive runs (night-shift TC1, reviewer TC7) to a monthly spot-check cadence; replace them with 2-3 new canaries derived from this week's real incidents — a session-limit mid-verification kill scenario (from the subagent-session-lifecycle gap) and a ~/.claude/ write-gate delegation scenario (from agent-os-self-modification-delegation); raise B2 dynamic eval count from 2 to 4 per night since incident-sourced evals (e.g., DYN-20260713-1 at 4.6 with concrete c3/c5 deductions) are the only ones still producing discriminating signal.

**Impact:** Eval suite regains discriminative power; per-night compute shifts from confirming known-good behavior to probing the 4 active capability gaps; baselines for new canaries establish within ~5 runs given the existing ESTABLISHING mechanism.

**Risk:** Retiring a saturated canary removes the tripwire for regression on that exact behavior — a future agent-file edit could silently reintroduce the failure; mitigate with the monthly spot-check cadence rather than full deletion, and auto-reinstate any canary whose spot-check drops below 4.5.

## P-2026-07-13-003: skill_gap

**Problem:** B3 high-severity gap 'subagent-session-lifecycle' with fresh evidence (well within 14 days): session limits killed 2 agents mid-verification on 2026-07-07 (kin Phase C, reports lost), a second builder kill within 24h on 2026-07-08 (tester-access sprint), and 3/7 subagents idling without final summaries requiring SendMessage re-pulls. Attribution data confirms: main-thread absorbed 3 of 4 capability gaps this week (top context: tester-access sprint). No mechanism warns before limits hit or checkpoints work-in-progress.

**Solution:** Create ~/.claude/rules/subagent-session-budget.md encoding: (a) preflight estimate of remaining session capacity before spawning long-running builder agents, (b) mandatory incremental progress trailers (checkpoint block appended to the subagent's report file after each completed unit) so work survives a mid-task kill, and (c) a standardized SendMessage recovery-pull sequence for idle/killed agents. Add a 3-line reference to the checkpoint requirement in ~/.claude/agents/developer.md and ~/.claude/agents/reviewer.md.

**Impact:** Eliminates the recurring lost-report/lost-verification failure (3+ events in 7d); main-thread stops paying a full recovery cycle per incident; independent verification survives session kills instead of being redone in-thread.

**Risk:** Checkpoint trailers add token overhead to every builder session even when no kill occurs, and a badly-tuned capacity estimate could make main-thread refuse to spawn agents it should spawn; mitigate by making the preflight advisory (warn, don't block) for the first two weeks and measuring checkpoint overhead in the A1 telemetry.

## P-2026-07-13-004: memory_consolidation

**Problem:** Two B6 consolidation findings are accumulating dead weight: (1) hook 'pre-response-claim-audit' last fired 2026-06-07 (36 days stale) and its only firing in the 7d window was a false positive (fp_rate=1.0, 0 valid catches per hook_rule_fp_rate_7d); (2) rule overlap between agent-delegation-triggers.md and cloudflare-deploy.md at 37% shared directives, which risks divergent edits — notably relevant since agent-delegation-triggers was the one rule with a valid catch this week.

**Solution:** Two changes: (1) disable or archive the pre-response-claim-audit hook (move its definition to ~/.claude/hooks/archive/ with a dated note citing 36-day staleness and 100% recent FP rate), keeping the file recoverable; (2) deduplicate /Users/reggie/.claude/rules/cloudflare-deploy.md by replacing its 37% shared directives with a single reference line pointing to /Users/reggie/.claude/rules/agent-delegation-triggers.md as the canonical source, keeping only Cloudflare-specific directives in place.

**Impact:** Removes a hook that currently only produces false positives (halving the FP contribution to hook_catches_7d), and establishes a single source of truth for delegation triggers so future edits propagate instead of diverging.

**Risk:** The stale hook may guard a rare-but-real failure mode that simply hasn't occurred in 36 days — archiving rather than deleting mitigates this; the rule dedup could break Cloudflare deploy flows if any of the 37% shared directives had context-specific wording, so the diff needs Hero review before applying.
